'''''Zealandorhynchus''''' is an extinct genus of [[billfish]] that lived around [[New Zealand]] during the early [[Eocene]] epoch. The only species found to be in this genus is '''''Zealandorhynchus fordycei'''''. 

It was named in honor of Professor [[Ewan Fordyce]], a [[Vertebrate paleontology|vertebrate paleontologist]] in New Zealand who had a 40-year long career in the [[University of Otago]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Otago |first=University of |date=2023-11-30 |title=Remembering Geology's paleontological powerhouse: Professor Ewan Fordyce |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/news/newsroom/remembering-geologys-paleontological-powerhouse-professor-ewan-fordyce |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=www.otago.ac.nz |language=en}}</ref>

== Phylogeny ==
Phylogenetic analysis of ''Z. fordycei'' has placed this species as a basal member of [[Billfish|Xiphioidei]] and part of the extinct family [[Xiphiorhynchidae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Rust |first1=Seabourne |last2=Wium |first2=Morne |last3=Otero |first3=Rodrigo A. |last4=Terezow |first4=Marianna |date=2026-02-01 |title=Fossil billfish (Xiphioidei) from the Eocene of Hampden, North Otago, New Zealand |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1342937X25003120 |journal=Gondwana Research |volume=150 |pages=301–311 |doi=10.1016/j.gr.2025.09.021 |bibcode=2026GondR.150..301R |issn=1342-937X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Discovery ==
The specimens for this species were collected in the [[Kurinui Formation]] from [[Hampden Beach, New Zealand|Hampden Beach]], [[North Otago]] region, [[South Island]] of [[New Zealand]]. From here, two large crania, with the first discovered in 1984, and the second discovered in two sections on 3 October 2020 and 10 November 2022 by Morne Mamlambo, belonging to billfishes were uncovered with the most complete material being referred to as ''Zealandorhynchus'' with the lesser complete material referred to as an unknown species of undetermined placement ([[incertae sedis|''incertae sedis'']]).<ref name=":0" /> They are currently house inside the [[Earth Science New Zealand National Paleontological]] Collection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Otago |first=University of |date=2025-11-10 |title=Ancient fossil named after legendary researcher |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/news/newsroom/ancient-fossil-named-after-legendary-researcher |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=www.otago.ac.nz |language=en}}</ref>

The discovery of ''Zealandorhynchus'' along with another ''incertae sedis'' Xiphioidei represents notable additions to the [[fossil record]] of fish species in New Zealand during the Eocene epoch. They also show that Xiphiorhynchidae reached a high level of diversity and widespread [[Southern Ocean]] distribution at the time. This means that even before the [[Oligocene|Oligocene epoch]], early species of billfishes already had a [[cosmopolitan distribution]].<ref name=":0" />
